questions.stem: The half-life of a radioactive nucleus is $5 \mathrm{years}$. The fraction of the original sample that will decay in $15 \mathrm{years}$ is $\frac{N}{8}$. The value of $N$ is:
questions.solution:
Number of half-lives $n = \frac{t}{T_{1/2}} = \frac{15}{5} = 3$.
Fraction of sample remaining $f_{\text{remain}} = \left(\frac{1}{2} \right)^3 = \frac{1}{8}$.
Fraction of sample decayed $f_{\text{decay}} = 1 - \frac{1}{8} = \frac{7}{8}$.
Comparing with $\frac{N}{8}$, we get $N = 7$.

questions.stem: A radioactive sample has a half-life of 10 days. The time (in days) required for the activity of the sample to decay to $12.5\%$ of its initial activity is ______.
questions.solution:
$12.5\%$ of initial activity is equivalent to $1/8$-th of the initial activity:
$\frac{A}{A_0} = 12.5\% = \frac{1}{8} = \left( \frac{1}{2} \right)^3$.
This corresponds to exactly 3 half-lives.
Total time: $t = 3 \times T_{1/2} = 3 \times 10\ \mathrm{days} = 30\ \mathrm{days}$.

questions.stem: A radioactive sample has a half-life of $10\ \mathrm{days}$. The fraction of the sample left undecayed after $40\ \mathrm{days}$ is $\frac{1}{N}$. The value of $N$ is _________.
questions.solution:
The number of half-lives is $n = \frac{t}{T_{1/2}} = \frac{40}{10} = 4$.
The remaining fraction is $N_t/N_0 = \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^n = \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^4 = \frac{1}{16}$.
Therefore, $N = 16$.

questions.stem: A radioactive sample has a half-life of $10\ \mathrm{days}$. The fraction of the sample that will remain undecayed after $30\ \mathrm{days}$ is:
questions.solution:
The number of half-lives is $n = \frac{t}{T_{1/2}} = \frac{30\ \mathrm{days}}{10\ \mathrm{days}} = 3$. 
The fraction of the sample remaining undecayed is: 
$\frac{N}{N_0} = \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^n = \left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^3 = \frac{1}{8}$.
